raw.rationale: Selamectin is a macrocyclic lactone anthelmintic that activates invertebrate glutamate-gated chloride channels and has no known cytotoxic target or antiproliferative mechanism in human cancer cells; at 2.5 µM for 5 days it is unlikely to produce lineage-selective killing, and any apparent activity would be nonspecific. Published PRISM data show no lineage-selective cytotoxicity for selamectin, so probabilities are near the low end of the base rate.
